append.text: **Ps 26:1b *a quo trepidábo?* → *diante de quem tremerei?*** — the stylist: *tremer de alguém* is not Portuguese; MS1932's preposition taken. The pair *a quem temerei? / diante de quem tremerei?* keeps the Latin's two verbs.
**Ps 26:9b *Adjútor meus esto* → *Sede o meu auxílio*** (a versicle, 05-01r.txt) — the Latinist's MAJOR *auxiliador* held again (D19/D24), as at 29:11. 27:7 (minor) the same.

**Ps 26:6b *Circuívi, et immolávi* (no object) → *Andei ao redor, e imolei*** — *rodear* is transitive in Portuguese and the stylist asked *rodeei o quê?*; without an object the going round is said with *andar ao redor* (circum- kept). With an object (117:10) *rodear* stands.

**Ps 26:10 *Dóminus autem assúmpsit me* → *o Senhor, porém, me recolheu*** — applied; the blind reader heard taking in (death a second hearing). *autem* → *porém* after the subject, where the Latin has it (the stylist).
**Ps 26:11 *dírige me in sémitam rectam* → *encaminhai-me à vereda reta*** — copied as the row directs; no remark.

**Ps 26:14 *Exspécta Dóminum … et sústine Dóminum* → *Aguarda o Senhor … e espera pelo Senhor*** — HANDOFF Open 14 decided with the three verbs kept apart (speráre in → esperar em, 26:3b *nisto eu esperarei*); the Greek has ὑπόμεινον twice, the Latin varies and the variation costs nothing; no reader objected. For Gustavo's review.
**Ps 26:14 *sústine Dóminum* → *espera pelo Senhor*** — see exspectáre: the three verbs apart.

**Ps 26:14 *et confortétur cor tuum* → *e que o teu coração se fortaleça*** — the jussive with *que* (the stylist: the inverted *fortaleça-se o teu coração* ceremonious); **30:25 *et confortétur cor vestrum* should copy (*e que o vosso coração se fortaleça*).**
**Ps 26:1b *Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ* → *O Senhor é o protetor da minha vida*** — applied.

**Ps 26:4 *hanc requíram* → *esta procurarei*; 26:8 *exquisívit te fácies mea: fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram* → *a minha face vos procurou: a vossa face, Senhor, procurarei*** (exquírere and requírere one verb, as the glossary merged them).

**Ps 26:4 departs, with a reason: *que eu habite*** — after *Uma coisa pedi ao Senhor, esta procurarei*, the ut-clause is what is asked (τοῦ κατοικεῖν; DRB *that I may dwell*), not a purpose; *para que* would be heard as the request made in order to dwell. The words after the conjunction are 22:6b's, so the echo stands; *para que eu habite* is the option. No reader remarked.

terms: | illuminátio | luz (*O Senhor é a minha luz e a minha salvação*) | open | Ps 26:1 (the Monday Prime antiphon; Introits) — God named as the one who gives light; *iluminação* makes him a process and is heard as lighting. Cost: *lumen* → luz too; they never meet in a verse (grep), but 4:7 *lumen vultus tui* and 43:4, 89:8 *illuminátio vultus tui* are near-formulas and may keep them apart with *iluminação* (free). DRB *light*, MS1932 *luz*. |

| nocéntes (participle as noun) | malfeitores (*os malfeitores*) | open | Ps 26:2 (κακοῦντας); only other place 34:1 *Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me*, where the object may ask for *os que me fazem mal*. Apart from malígnus → malvado (D24), iníquus → iníquo, ímpius → ímpio. |

| castra | acampamento (*Se um acampamento se instalar contra mim*) | open | Ps 26:3 (παρεμβολή; the Eastertide responsory, Pasc2-3.txt); the Latin names the camp, not the army. *consístere* → *instalar-se* here (the stylist wanted the subject first; *postar* unknown to the blind reader and heard today as posting online). 26:3b turned the same way (*Se uma batalha se levantar contra mim*). Other *castra*: 77:28, 105:16 (grep before copying). |

| voluptas | delícias (*as delícias do Senhor*) | open | Ps 26:4b; 35:9 *torrénte voluptátis tuæ*. *deleite* is delectátio's, *doçura* dulcédo's, *prazer* heard first as the senses' (and 25:3 has *achei prazer* for complacére). The Latinist (minor) wants the singular *o prazer*; refused, the plural is the idiom (number is grammar), *a delícia* an option. delíciæ 138:11 decides there. |

| *in abscóndito* (a hidden place) | *no lugar escondido* (*protegeu-me no lugar escondido da sua tenda*) | open | Ps 26:5, keeping *abscóndit … in abscóndito* (ἔκρυψεν … ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ) one root; *esconderijo* is latíbulum's (17:12) — the stylist's word, refused, an option; 9:30a's adverbial *às escondidas* is another use. **30:21 *Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ* should follow.** |

| petra | rocha (*Sobre uma rocha me exaltou*) | open | Ps 26:6; *lapis* → pedra (117:22). Indefinite, as the Latin has no article. **60:3 *In petra exaltásti me* should copy.** 12 other lines (grep: 39:3, 60:3, 77:15, 77:16, 77:20, 80:17, 103:12, 103:17, 104:41, 113:8, 136:9, 140:6). |

| hóstia | vítima (*uma vítima de aclamação*) | open | Ps 26:6b; the cognate *hóstia* is heard first as the Host, *sacrifício* is sacrifícium's (115:17 *tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis*, DO id 115:7b, has both roots, so they must differ). The blind reader heard *vítima* as someone harmed (he did not know *imolei*) — the cost, recorded. Other *hóstia*: 95:8 *Tóllite hóstias*, 115:17 (DO id 115:7b) — grep. |
| vociferátio | aclamação | open | Ps 26:6b *hóstiam vociferatiónis*; 32:3 *bene psállite ei in vociferatióne* can follow. ἀλαλαγμός, the shout. *júbilo* left to gáudium / jubilátio (46:6). |

| viríliter ágere | portar-se como homem (*porta-te como homem*) | open | Ps 26:14; **30:25 *Viríliter ágite* → *Portai-vos como homens*** (only the two, grep). Draft 1 had MS1932's *porta-te varonilmente*: the blind reader did not know *varonilmente*, the stylist (worst line) called it bookish and asked *age como homem*; his *como homem* taken (the Latin's vir), the verb kept for 30:25, where *Agi* is also 'I acted' (rule 3). |
formulas: | *Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea: quem timébo?* (26:1; the Monday Prime antiphon *Illuminátio mea * et salus mea Dóminus*, Psalmi minor.txt; Introits Pent04-0 and others) | *O Senhor é a minha luz e a minha salvação: a quem temerei?* — the antiphon in its own order: *A minha luz * e a minha salvação é o Senhor* | open — Ps 26 |

| *Credo vidére bona Dómini in terra vivéntium* (26:13; antiphon of the Office of the Dead and Holy Saturday, Commune/C9.txt, Quad6-6.txt) | *Creio que verei os bens do Senhor * na terra dos vivos* | open — Ps 26; **the Latinist's MAJOR (*Creio ver*) held**: *Creio ver* is heard as 'I think I see' |

| *Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum* (26:14; Gradual of Tuesday in Passion Week, Quad5-2.txt) | *Aguarda o Senhor, porta-te como homem: * e que o teu coração se fortaleça, e espera pelo Senhor* | open — Ps 26 (HANDOFF Open 14) |

| *Insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui. R. Et mentíta est iníquitas sibi* (26:12b; the Passiontide responsory, Quad6-5.txt, Minor Special.txt) | *Levantaram-se contra mim testemunhas iníquas. R. E a iniquidade mentiu a si mesma.* | open — Ps 26 |
